items.item_text: This position requires a minimum of two (2) days/week on campus/on-site.
Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.
Occasional evenings and weekends may be required.

Mandated reporter under CANRA. Duties may require direct contact with children (defined as individuals under the age of 18). Completion of the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA) form will be required.
Cover letter required for a complete application.

Demonstrated knowledge and hands-on experience managing international scholar services, including proficiency in visa procedures (e.g., J-1, H-1B, OPT/STEM OPT), policies, immigration laws pertaining to foreign scholars, appointment workflows and onboarding.

Reporting to the Academic Personnel Manager, the incumbent is directly responsible for academic HR functions of multiple engineering departments. Uses professional academic HR concepts as a seasoned, experienced academic HR professional to apply organization policies and procedures to resolve the full range of academic HR-related issues. Works on problems that are diverse and complex in scope, where analysis of situations requires a review of a variety of factors. Independently manage all departmental/personnel matters related to academic personnel, employee relations, labor relations, classification and compensation, recruitment, payroll and timekeeping for assigned areas. Manages a wide variety of complex issues, exercises leadership, discretionary authority, high level of creativity, negotiation, investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Serve as a team lead and advise the Academic Personnel Manager on academic HR matters. Serve as an escalation point from other team members to the Academic Personnel Manager or central campus departments. Formulate or participate in formulating management policies on the full spectrum of imperative and strategic academic HR topics. Develop, interpret, implement and revise policies, procedures, and guidelines. Provide counsel and present information in clear terms to managers and employees. Plan, implement and conduct statistical analyses and produce analytic reports relevant to department policymaking or procedures. Create, implement and maintain effective systems of internal and external coordination. This position supports a collaborative, cross-functional environment by cross-training with other team members and providing backup coverage across sections as needed to maintain continuity of operations and consistent academic HR support across the Jacobs School of Engineering.

Interacts regularly with Jacobs School of Engineering departments, Central Campus units (such Academic Personnel Services, Employee Relations, and Labor Relations), and internal stakeholders to provide policy interpretation, academic reviews and resolve a wide variety of academic HR issues of complex scope and complexity. The role contributes to improving processes, workflows, and service delivery across the Jacobs School of Engineering.
Oversee special projects and other duties as assigned. Provide backup support to other team members.
In the absence of the Academic Personnel Manager, this position may serve as backup.
~ Cover letter required for a complete application.
Excellent critical and innovative thinking to address moderately complex issues and present nuanced analyses.
Requires thorough knowledge of and ability to apply / interpret organization and college policies and procedures which govern academic HR.
Thorough knowledge of organization and college goals, priorities and values and the legal and human implications of decisions.

Thorough knowledge of systemwide and organization policies, union contracts, procedures and practices that govern academic HR administration. Ability to analyze documents for compliance with University regulations and procedures; Unit 18 MOU regulations and procedures; Affirmative Action Guidelines; and immigration regulations.
Knowledge of trends in academia, especially in areas of academic planning, human resource management and administration.

Ability to analyze complex management issues, develop project scope and solutions, give professional advice to senior officials, and make critical decisions regarding personnel. Analytical skills to conduct analysis and develop recommendations to Chairs / unit management.
Ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences.

Demonstrated proficiency with business software including word processing, spreadsheets, email and calendaring systems. Demonstrated ability to learn and use specialized or proprietary systems and applications and the ability to update and expand skills as needed.
Knowledge and understanding of the structure of large organizations and how to effectively operate to accomplish goals and develop new initiatives/programs within this framework.
Demonstrated organization, problem solving, and communication skills.

Ability to work independently, exercising initiative and judgment in the performance of a broad range of responsibilities in an environment of routinely sensitive and confidential issues with the acumen and sensitivity to identify those decisions and activities which require confidentiality and/or higher-level consultation and/or group collaboration.

Attention to detail and ability to follow through on both independent and group projects, understanding the philosophy of quality service and cooperative group process, while displaying proven aptitude for both solitary and team-related endeavors.
Ability to proof, draft, edit and make recommendations for correspondence and written materials. Ability to write and speak concisely and persuasively.
Knowledge of visa rules and guidelines and ability to interpret and communicate guidelines effectively.
Willingness and demonstrated ability to embrace and consistently uphold the principles of community for a collaborative work environment.
Skill in developing and efficiently maintaining accurate record keeping systems.

Demonstrated theoretical and practical knowledge of UC academic policies and procedures needed to coordinate and advise on academic personnel issues; ability to research, advise or consult with Academic Personnel Manager, Dean and/or Associate Deans to propose creative solutions in line with divisional objectives.
Ability to use project management platforms (such as ClickUp) to streamline HR workflows, track deliverables, ensure accountability and optimize operations.
